newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Asia businessmen urge APEC to press for free trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia businessmen urge APEC to press for free trade.

text.p: Business leaders in Asia and Pacific countries urged the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation panel (APEC) on Monday to do more to carry out its free trade policies.

"(We) call on APEC to move in 1997 from an agenda-setting body to an implementation body with specific, concrete and measurable outcomes," Robert Lees, secretary general of the Pacific Basin Economic Council (PBEC) told the council's annual meeting in Manila.
APEC groups 18 economies in the Pacific Rim that aim to bring down trade and investment barriers by 2010 for developed economies and 2020 for developing economies.
But the group does not impose a strict timetable on specific industries for its members to follow.
PBEC chairman Gary Tooker said a slowdown in maturing economies might drive some governments to go slow or even reverse their liberalisation agenda.
"Progress that we've seen in breaking down barriers in global commerce can be quickly reversed...We need to encourage APEC forward to meaningful actions," he said.

Among the priorities the group wants APEC to focus on include the elimination of administrative barriers to trade and investment, meeting World Trade Organisation commitments, and establishing protection of intellectual property rights.
Philippine President Fidel Ramos, who hosted the fourth APEC leaders' meeting in Subic last November, welcomed the suggestions.
"I believe that within the APEC framework we can build a stronger strategic alliance between government and business," he said.
"APEC is not just a talk shop as its critics say, APEC means business. And APEC means action," he added.
